chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abi Ishaq, from Abdullah ibn al-Husayn ibn Zayd ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام, from his father, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

A woman does not wipe the head as men wipe. Rather, when a woman enters the morning, she wipes her head and removes the khimar from it; then when it is Zuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha, she wipes over her forelock.

key_terms.الرَّأْسِ: the head, the place of wiping in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الْخِمَارَ: the head covering worn by a woman
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman, the subject of the legal ruling
key_terms.بِنَاصِيَتِهَا: with her forelock, meaning the front part of her head/hair
key_terms.تَمْسَحُ: she wipes, referring here to the prescribed wiping in wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: How does a woman wipe her head in wudu (ablution) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning how a woman performs the wiping of the head in wudu (ablution). It distinguishes her practice from that of men, indicating a concession related to her head covering and specifying wiping the forelock in later prayers.
